To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

differential time and money pricing as a mechanism for in-kind redistribution can achieve the distributional goal "specific egalitarian", or that allocation be independent of income but increasing in strength of need or preference, more efficiently than uniform provision funded from income taxes, with or without the option to purchase privately.
differential pricing is a mechanism that implements the distributional goal "specific egalitarian" in the context of a public good and that it is more efficient than uniform public provision.
differential time and money pricing can be a very effective mechanism for redistributing goods and services in-kind.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a specific mechanism for implementing specific egalitarianism, and with the conditions under which this mechanism becomes more efficient than other methods for achieving the same objective.
the design of policies that can achieve a distributional goal of egalitarianism.
the design of a pricing mechanism to achieve a specific egalitarian distribution of a good.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

differential pricing is more efficient than uniform public provision when the good is relatively more important, when income inequality is higher or when the proportion of the population who are poor is lower.
differential pricing is a mechanism to implement specific egalitarianism that is more efficient than public provision, funded from income tax and with private purchase optional.
differential pricing is a mechanism that has the potential to improve on uniform pricing in many circumstances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

differential pricing can improve the efficiency of in-kind redistribution, especially in situations where the relative importance of redistribution increases, the relative importance of other goods decreases, income inequality rises and/or the proportion of poor people falls.
differential pricing is a mechanism to redistribute in kind.
the optimal policy is a combination of differential pricing and public provision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
differential time and money pricing is an important mechanism for in-kind redistribution.
differential time and money pricing can be used to redistribute in-kind, without the need to know individual incomes.
governments should be open to the idea of differential time and money prices as a way of achieving redistributional goals.
